editorial:
Imagine your perfect life suddenly blowing up in your face. That is exactly what happens to Mary Haines when she finds out her husband is cheating on her. You get to follow her through a world of high-society gossip and fancy parties where every woman has an opinion on her misery. The vibe is like a glamorous soap opera, focusing on the bonds and betrayals between female friends. It feels like you are eavesdropping on a private conversation between wealthy ladies who love to talk behind each other's backs.

Since this is a filmed version of a Broadway play, the acting is top-notch and feels very natural. The dialogue is snappy and funny, keeping you hooked even when the drama gets heavy. The only downside is that it can feel a bit like a stage show since there are not many location changes. If you love sharp wit and emotional growth, you should definitely check this out. You can easily rent it on Apple TV or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best picture quality for those gorgeous costumes.
endingExplained: After a lot of fighting and tears, Mary realizes she cannot rely on her fake friends for happiness. She finally confronts her husband and decides to stop playing the victim. Instead of just begging for him to stay, she finds her own strength and confidence. The movie wraps up with Mary feeling empowered and independent, showing that she is stronger on her own than she ever was in a lie.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves witty dialogue and stories about female friendships.
